fact: Innate immunity gives continuous barrier defense and reacts to microbes in the first hours or days of infection, before adaptive responses develop.
quote: provides continuous barrier defenses to prevent infection and also reacts to invading microbes in the first few hours or days after infection

fact: The innate immune system is fully functional before an infection occurs.
quote: The innate immune system is fully functional in individuals even before an infection occurs

fact: Adaptive immunity is stimulated by exposure to infectious agents and increases in magnitude and defensive capability with repeated exposure.
quote: increase in magnitude and defensive capabilities with repeated exposures to a particular microbe

fact: The innate response gives early danger signals that stimulate adaptive responses, and adaptive responses often enhance innate protective mechanisms.
quote: The innate immune response to microbes provides early danger signals that stimulate adaptive immune responses.

fact: The kinetics of innate and adaptive responses are approximations and vary between infections.
quote: The kinetics of the innate and adaptive immune responses are approximations and may vary in different infections.

fact: Innate immunity is specific for molecules shared by groups of related microbes and for molecules from damaged host cells; adaptive immunity is specific for many microbial and nonmicrobial antigens.
quote: For molecules shared by groups of related microbes and molecules produced by damaged host cells

fact: Innate diversity is low because germline genes encode the recognition molecules; adaptive diversity is very high because of somatic recombination of gene segments.
quote: Low; recognition molecules encoded by inherited (germline) genes

fact: Innate immunity has limited memory; adaptive immunity has memory.
quote: Memory Limited Yes

fact: Both innate and adaptive immunity show nonreactivity to self.
quote: Nonreactivity to self Yes Yes

fact: Innate components are epithelia, antimicrobial molecules, complement, lectins, phagocytes, dendritic cells, NK cells, mast cells, eosinophils and ILCs; adaptive components are B and T lymphocytes and antibodies.
quote: Phagocytes (macrophages, neutrophils), dendritic cells, natural killer cells, mast cells, eosinophils, innate lymphoid cells

fact: Innate responses to repeated exposure to the same microbe are usually the same in kinetics, magnitude and quality as the first response.
quote: the kinetics, magnitude, and qualities of innate responses to repeated exposures of the same microbe are usually the same as after the first exposure

fact: Dendritic cells, some macrophages and mast cells are resident in most tissues and act as sentinels.
quote: Innate immune cells, including DCs, some macrophages, and mast cells, are resident in most tissues, and they function as sentinels

fact: Innate immunity combats microbes by inflammation (recruitment of leukocytes) and by blocking viral replication or killing virus-infected cells.
quote: by recruiting phagocytes and other leukocytes that destroy the microbes, in the process called inflammation

fact: Lymphocyte activation and differentiation take several days, so the adaptive response is slow and innate immunity must protect first.
quote: take several days, which explains why the adaptive response is slow to develop and innate immunity has to provide protection initially

fact: Secondary adaptive responses are usually more rapid, greater in magnitude and often qualitatively different from the primary response.
quote: more rapid, greater in magnitude, and often qualitatively different from the first, or primary, immune response to that antigen

fact: Innate immunity recognizes about 1000 products of microbes and damaged cells; adaptive immunity can recognize millions of antigens.
quote: the innate immune system recognizes only about 1000 products of microbes and damaged cells

fact: Innate immunity uses germline-encoded invariant receptors; adaptive immunity uses diverse receptors from somatically rearranged genes.
quote: The innate immune system uses germline-encoded invariant receptors to recognize microbial and other products.

fact: Microbial substances that stimulate innate immunity are often shared by classes of microbes and are called PAMPs.
quote: are often shared by classes of microbes and are called pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs)

fact: DAMPs are endogenous molecules released from damaged or dying cells, including cells injured by sterile insults such as burns or trauma.
quote: These substances are called damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs)

fact: Cells that die by apoptosis generally do not release DAMPs.
quote: DAMPs are generally not released from cells dying by apoptosis.

fact: Innate immunity recognizes microbial products that are often essential for microbial survival, so microbes usually cannot evade it by losing them.
quote: microbes usually cannot evade innate immunity by eliminating molecules that may be recognized by the host

fact: Some cytokines released from damaged cells are DAMPs called alarmins.
quote: are sometimes called alarmins because their presence outside cells sends an alarm to the immune system

fact: Innate immunity uses fewer than 100 types of invariant receptors; adaptive immunity uses only two receptor types (Ig and TCR) with millions of variants.
quote: <100 different types of invariant receptors

fact: Innate receptors are nonclonal (identical on all cells of a lineage); adaptive receptors are clonal.
quote: Nonclonal: identical receptors on all cells of the same lineage

fact: Adaptive self-nonreactivity depends on elimination or inactivation of self-reactive lymphocytes and may be imperfect, giving rise to autoimmunity.
quote: based on elimination or inactivation of self-reactive lymphocytes; may be imperfect (giving rise to autoimmunity)

fact: Innate immunity ignores healthy cells because normal cells lack most ligands, receptors sit in separate compartments, and regulatory proteins block activation.
quote: normal cells do not produce ligands for most innate immune receptors

fact: Defects in innate components are very rare but increase susceptibility to infection even when adaptive immunity is intact.
quote: defects in its components, which are very rare, can lead to increased susceptibility to infection, even in the presence of an intact adaptive immune system

fact: The main interfaces with the environment are the skin and the mucosal surfaces of the gastrointestinal, respiratory and genitourinary tracts.
quote: the skin and the mucosal surfaces of the gastrointestinal, respiratory, and genitourinary tracts

fact: Loss of epithelial integrity predisposes to infection, and infection of barrier epithelial cells is a frequent first event in barrier breakdown.
quote: Loss of the integrity of these epithelial layers by trauma or other reasons predisposes an individual to infections

fact: Epithelial cells form tight junctions that block the passage of microbes between cells.
quote: The epithelial cells form tight junctions with one another, blocking the passage of microbes between the cells.

fact: The outer keratin layer of skin blocks microbial penetration, and skin infections usually occur after a barrier breach.
quote: cutaneous infections generally occur when there is a barrier breach

fact: Respiratory, gastrointestinal and genitourinary epithelia produce mucus containing mucins, which physically impairs microbial invasion.
quote: Mucus, a viscous secretion containing glycoproteins called mucins, is produced by respiratory, gastrointestinal, and urogenital epithelial cells

fact: Ciliary action in the bronchial tree and peristalsis in the gut help to eliminate microbes.
quote: ciliary action in the bronchial tree and by peristalsis in the gut, which facilitate elimination of microbes

fact: In cystic fibrosis, thick mucus or impaired ciliary movement leads to lung infections by bacteria that colonize the epithelial surface but do not cross it.
quote: Such individuals frequently develop lung infections caused by bacteria that colonize the epithelial surface but do not cross it.

fact: Failure of peristalsis is typically accompanied by overgrowth of pathogenic bacteria in the gut lumen.
quote: Failure of peristalsis is typically accompanied by the overgrowth of pathogenic bacteria within the lumen of the gut.

fact: Surface epithelia provide mechanical, chemical and microbiological barriers to infection.
quote: Surface epithelia provide mechanical, chemical, and microbiological barriers to infection.

fact: Phagocytes lie beneath all epithelial surfaces and engulf invading microorganisms.
quote: the phagocytes that lie beneath all epithelial surfaces and that engulf and digest invading microorganisms

fact: Stomach acid, digestive enzymes, bile salts, fatty acids and lysolipids form a chemical barrier in the upper gastrointestinal tract.
quote: the acid pH of the stomach and the digestive enzymes, bile salts, fatty acids, and lysolipids present in the upper gastrointestinal tract

fact: Lysozyme (a glycosidase) and secretory phospholipase A2 are secreted in tears and saliva and by phagocytes; Paneth cells also make both.
quote: secreted in tears and saliva and by phagocytes. Lysozyme is a glycosidase ... Lysozyme is also produced by Paneth cells

fact: Lysozyme cleaves peptidoglycan and is more effective against Gram-positive than Gram-negative bacteria, whose LPS outer layer covers the peptidoglycan.
quote: is more effective against Gram-positive bacteria, in which the peptidoglycan cell wall is exposed

fact: Three important classes of antimicrobial peptides in mammals are defensins, cathelicidins and histatins.
quote: Three important classes of antimicrobial peptides in mammals are defensins, cathelicidins, and histatins.

fact: Defensins are cationic and hydrophobic peptides of 29 to 34 amino acids with three disulfide bonds; humans have alpha and beta families.
quote: Defensins are peptides, 29 to 34 amino acids long, that contain both cationic and hydrophobic regions and three intrachain disulfide bonds

fact: Defensins act within minutes to disrupt membranes of bacteria, fungi and some enveloped viruses.
quote: Defensins act within minutes to disrupt the cell membranes of bacteria, fungi, and the membrane envelopes of some viruses.

fact: Mucosal epithelial cells and granule-containing leukocytes (neutrophils, NK cells, CTLs) produce defensins.
quote: produced by epithelial cells of mucosal surfaces and by granule-containing leukocytes, including neutrophils, NK cells, and cytotoxic T lymphocytes

fact: Paneth cells in the crypts of the small bowel are a major source of alpha-defensins.
quote: Paneth cells within the crypts of the small bowel are a major producer of α-defensins.

fact: Beta-defensins are generally made in response to microbial products, mainly by epithelia of the respiratory and urogenital tracts, skin and tongue.
quote: are generally produced specifically in response to the presence of microbial products

fact: The single human theta-defensin gene is inactivated by a mutation.
quote: the single human 0-defensin gene has been inactivated by a mutation

fact: Neutrophils and barrier epithelia of skin, gut and airway make cathelicidin as an 18-kD precursor that is cleaved into two active peptides.
quote: is synthesized as an 18-kD precursor protein that is secreted and then proteolytically cleaved into two peptides

fact: The C-terminal cathelicidin fragment LL-37 binds and neutralizes LPS.
quote: The C-terminal fragment, called LL-37, can bind and neutralize LPS

fact: DNA-bound LL-37 activates plasmacytoid dendritic cells to secrete type I IFNs, and LL-37 may be an autoantigen in psoriasis.
quote: LL-37 may also be an autoantigen in human autoimmune diseases such as psoriasis.

fact: Neutrophils store cathelicidin propeptides in secondary granules, and elastase from primary granules activates them in the phagosome.
quote: the cathelicidin propeptides are stored in the secondary granules

fact: Parotid, sublingual and submandibular glands make histatins, which act against Cryptococcus neoformans and Candida albicans.
quote: are active against pathogenic fungi such as Cryptococcus neoformans and Candida albicans

fact: Antimicrobial peptides are usually made as inactive proproteins that need proteolytic cleavage for activity.
quote: Antimicrobial peptides are usually made as an inactive proprotein that requires a proteolytic step to complete its activation

fact: Barrier epithelia contain intraepithelial T lymphocytes (alpha-beta or gamma-delta TCR) with limited receptor diversity.
quote: A characteristic of intraepithelial T cells is the limited diversity of their antigen receptors

fact: Commensal microbiota compete with pathogens for nutrients and for attachment sites on epithelial cells.
quote: compete with pathogenic microorganisms for nutrients and for attachment sites on epithelial cells

fact: Microbiota produce antimicrobial substances, such as lactic acid from vaginal lactobacilli and bacteriocins.
quote: such as the lactic acid produced by vaginal lactobacilli, some strains of which also produce antimicrobial peptides (bacteriocins)

fact: Commensals strengthen the barrier by stimulating epithelial cells to make antimicrobial peptides.
quote: by stimulating the epithelial cells to produce antimicrobial peptides

fact: When antibiotics kill commensals, pathogens frequently replace them and cause disease.
quote: When commensal microorganisms are killed by antibiotic treatment, pathogens frequently replace them and cause disease

fact: Commensals can cause disease if their growth is not controlled or if the immune system is compromised.
quote: commensal microbes themselves can cause disease if their growth is not kept in check or if the immune system is compromised

fact: The response to a new pathogen has three phases: immediate innate (0-4 h), early induced innate (4-96 h) and adaptive (>96 h).
quote: (immediate: 0-4 hours) ... (early: 4-96 hours) ... (late: >96 hours)

fact: Immediate defenses are preformed soluble molecules such as lysozyme, defensins and complement.
quote: These first defenses include several classes of preformed soluble molecules present in blood, extracellular fluid, and epithelial secretions

fact: In the second phase, innate cells recognize PAMPs and become activated.
quote: these innate immune cells sense the presence of a pathogen by recognizing molecules typical of a microbe

fact: Neither soluble nor cellular innate components generate long-term protective memory.
quote: neither the soluble nor the cellular components of innate immunity generate long-term protective immunological memory

fact: Adaptive immunity is late because rare specific B and T cells must first expand clonally; effector mechanisms are similar in each phase.
quote: The effector mechanisms that remove the infectious agent are similar or identical in each phase.

fact: In the induced phase of innate immunity, an inflammatory response often first counters the spread of a pathogen.
quote: In the second, induced, phase of the innate immune response, the spread of a pathogen is often initially countered by an inflammatory response

fact: Induced innate responses act over several days while dendritic cells carry antigen to local lymphoid tissue to start the adaptive response.
quote: The induced responses of innate immunity act over several days

fact: Innate defenses act within minutes, and an adaptive response is needed only when innate defenses are bypassed, evaded or overwhelmed.
quote: Only when the innate host defenses have been bypassed, evaded, or overwhelmed is an adaptive immune response required.

fact: Innate immunity keeps pathogen numbers in check while the adaptive response develops.
quote: the innate immune system performs a valuable delaying function, keeping pathogen numbers in check

fact: Acute inflammation is the accumulation of leukocytes, plasma proteins and fluid from the blood at an extravascular site of infection or injury.
quote: accumulation of leukocytes, plasma proteins, and fluid derived from the blood at an extravascular tissue site of infection or injury

fact: Innate immunity protects by inducing inflammation, inducing antiviral defense and stimulating adaptive immunity.
quote: are by inducing inflammation, inducing antiviral defense, and stimulating adaptive immunity

fact: Tissue sentinel cells (macrophages, DCs, mast cells) and epithelial cells start acute inflammation after recognition of PAMPs or DAMPs.
quote: mainly macrophages, DCs, and mast cells, as well as by epithelial barrier cells

fact: Inflammation delivers effector molecules and cells, induces local clotting, and promotes tissue repair.
quote: Inflammation has three essential roles in combating infection.

fact: Inflammation is characterized by pain, redness, heat and swelling at the site of infection.
quote: Inflammatory responses are operationally characterized by pain, redness, heat, and swelling at the site of an infection

fact: Vasodilation increases local blood flow (heat and redness) and slows flow along vessel walls.
quote: leading to increased local blood flow—hence the heat and redness

fact: Activated endothelium expresses adhesion molecules, and leukocytes attach and migrate into tissue (extravasation).
quote: allows leukocytes to attach to the endothelium and migrate into the tissues, a process known as extravasation

fact: Increased vascular permeability causes swelling (edema) and pain and brings plasma proteins such as complement and MBL into tissue.
quote: accounts for the swelling, or edema, and pain

fact: Clotting in microvessels at the infection site prevents spread of the pathogen through the blood.
quote: prevents the spread of the pathogen via the blood

fact: Macrophages and neutrophils secrete lipid mediators: prostaglandins, leukotrienes and platelet-activating factor (PAF).
quote: secrete lipid mediators of inflammation—prostaglandins, leukotrienes, and platelet-activating factor (PAF)

fact: Tissue injury activates the kinin system, which produces bradykinin; bradykinin increases vascular permeability and causes pain.
quote: Bradykinin causes an increase in vascular permeability that promotes the influx of plasma proteins

fact: C5a increases vascular permeability and activates mast cells to release histamine and TNF.
quote: C5a also activates local mast cells

fact: Mast cells respond to PAMPs and DAMPs with histamine and prostaglandins, which cause vasodilation and increased capillary permeability.
quote: Mast cells respond to PAMPs and DAMPs by secreting histamine and prostaglandins that cause vasodilation and increased capillary permeability

fact: TNF and IL-1 induce endothelial E-selectin, ICAM-1 and VCAM-1 and stimulate chemokines such as CXCL8 and CCL2.
quote: Expression of E-selectin and ligands for integrins, including intercellular adhesion molecule 1 (ICAM-1) and vascular cell adhesion molecule 1 (VCAM-1)

fact: Neutrophils arrive first because they are the most abundant leukocytes and the most rapid responders; monocytes become more numerous over time and may dominate some reactions because they live longer and can proliferate locally.
quote: may be the dominant population in some reactions because they have longer lifespans than neutrophils and are capable of local proliferation

fact: Acute inflammation develops in minutes to hours and lasts for days.
quote: Acute inflammation develops in minutes to hours and lasts for days.

fact: Chronic inflammation follows if infection or injury persists; it involves monocytes and lymphocytes, angiogenesis and fibrosis.
quote: It usually involves recruitment and activation of monocytes and lymphocytes.

fact: TNF, IL-1 and IL-6 are three of the most important proinflammatory cytokines of innate immunity; innate cytokines are made mainly by tissue macrophages and DCs.
quote: Three of the most important proinflammatory cytokines of the innate immune system are TNF, IL-1

fact: Epithelial IL-25, TSLP and IL-33 stimulate ILC2s, Th2 cells and mast cells, and contribute to allergic disease; IL-33 is an alarmin.
quote: It is often called an alarmin because it is rapidly released from damaged epithelial cells

fact: Inadequate TNF, for example with TNF-blocking drugs, may cause failure to contain infections.
quote: a consequence may be failure to contain infections

fact: TNF and IL-1 act on the hypothalamus to cause fever and are called endogenous pyrogens.
quote: These cytokines are therefore called endogenous pyrogens

fact: Prostaglandin synthesis inhibitors such as aspirin reduce fever by blocking the cytokine effect.
quote: Prostaglandin synthesis inhibitors, such as aspirin, reduce fever by blocking this action of the cytokines.

fact: Endogenous pyrogens (TNF-alpha, IL-1beta, IL-6) induce cyclooxygenase-2 and prostaglandin E2; PGE2 acts on the hypothalamus to increase heat production and vasoconstriction.
quote: Endogenous pyrogens cause fever by inducing the synthesis of prostaglandin E2 by the enzyme cyclooxygenase-2

fact: LPS is an exogenous pyrogen that also induces cyclooxygenase-2 directly through TLR4 signaling.
quote: directly inducing cyclooxygenase-2 as a consequence of signaling through TLR-4

fact: The role of fever in host defense is not well understood.
quote: The role of fever in host defense is not well understood

fact: Fever is generally beneficial because most pathogens grow better at lower temperatures and adaptive responses are more intense at higher temperatures.
quote: Fever is generally beneficial to host defense; most pathogens grow better at lower temperatures

fact: TNF, IL-1 and IL-6 act on the bone marrow, with colony-stimulating factors, to cause leukocytosis.
quote: leading to elevated numbers of these white cells in the blood (leukocytosis)

fact: TNF, IL-1 and IL-6 induce hepatocytes to make acute-phase proteins such as CRP, SAP and fibrinogen; raised CRP is a clinical sign of inflammation.
quote: Elevated plasma CRP is used clinically as a sign of an inflammatory process.

fact: Plasma CRP can increase up to 1000-fold in infection because IL-6, IL-1 and TNF increase its synthesis by liver cells.
quote: can increase up to 1000-fold during infections and in response to other inflammatory stimuli

fact: CRP, SAP and PTX3 activate the classical complement pathway by binding C1q.
quote: CRP, SAP, and PTX3 all activate the classical pathway of complement by binding C1q.

fact: PTX3 is made by DCs, macrophages and endothelial cells and is also stored in neutrophil granules.
quote: PTX3 is also stored in neutrophil granules and released as neutrophils die

fact: In the acute-phase response, blood levels of some proteins go down while others increase markedly.
quote: blood levels of some proteins go down, whereas levels of others increase markedly

fact: CRP is a pentraxin that binds phosphocholine on bacterial and fungal surfaces but not in host membranes; it opsonizes and binds C1q.
quote: it binds to the phosphocholine portion of certain bacterial and fungal cell-wall lipopolysaccharides

fact: MBL is low in healthy blood and increases during the acute-phase response.
quote: MBL is present in low levels in the blood of healthy individuals

fact: Surfactant proteins SP-A and SP-D increase in the acute-phase response and promote phagocytosis of pathogens such as Pneumocystis jirovecii.
quote: important in promoting the phagocytosis of opportunistic respiratory pathogens such as Pneumocystis jirovecii

fact: Within a day or two, acute-phase proteins give antibody-like functions, but they have no structural diversity and are induced nonspecifically.
quote: acute-phase proteins have no structural diversity

fact: Janeway lists serum amyloid P as an acute-phase protein in mice but not in humans.
quote: serum amyloid protein (SAP) (in mice but not humans)

fact: Sepsis shows fever, fast heart and respiratory rates, metabolic abnormalities and mental disturbance, often started by LPS or lipoteichoic acid.
quote: clinically characterized by fever, fast heart and respiratory rates, metabolic abnormalities, and mental disturbances

fact: In septic shock, high TNF causes vascular collapse and disseminated intravascular coagulation.
quote: there is vascular collapse and disseminated intravascular coagulation, caused by the effects of high doses of TNF

fact: Systemic TNF reduces myocardial contractility and vascular tone, causes intravascular thrombosis and, if prolonged, cachexia.
quote: TNF inhibits myocardial contractility and vascular smooth muscle tone

fact: Clinical trials of anti-TNF antibodies or soluble TNF receptors have not shown benefit in sepsis.
quote: have not shown a benefit in patients with sepsis

fact: A septic-shock-like syndrome after burns, trauma or pancreatitis is called the systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS).
quote: This has been called the systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS).

fact: TNF blockade can reactivate tuberculosis in apparently well patients with previous infection, which shows the role of TNF in keeping infection local.
quote: these treatments have been found to reactivate tuberculosis in some apparently well patients with evidence of previous infection

fact: Lymphocyte activation needs two signals: antigen (signal 1) and molecules made during innate responses (signal 2).
quote: The activation of lymphocytes requires two distinct signals, the first being antigen

fact: Signal 1 makes the response specific; signal 2 makes sure adaptive responses start for dangerous infections and not for harmless or self antigens.
quote: ensures that adaptive immune responses are induced when there is a dangerous infection and not when lymphocytes recognize harmless antigens

fact: Second signals are costimulators (T cells), cytokines (T and B cells) and complement breakdown products (B cells).
quote: costimulators (for T cells), cytokines (for both T and B cells), and complement breakdown products (for B cells)

fact: Second signals increase the magnitude of the adaptive response and also influence its type.
quote: not only enhance the magnitude of the subsequent adaptive immune response but also influence the nature of the adaptive response

fact: IL-12 drives Th1; IL-1, IL-6 and IL-23 drive Th17; IL-25, IL-33 and TSLP drive Th2; IL-15 supports memory CD8+ T cells; IL-6 supports plasma cells.
quote: IL-25, IL-33, and TSLP stimulate the differentiation of naive CD4+ T cells to the Th2 subset of effector cells

fact: Blood-borne microbes activate the alternative complement pathway, and complement products enhance antibody production by B cells.
quote: some of the proteolytic products of complement activation enhance the production of antibodies by B lymphocytes

fact: Adjuvants work mostly by stimulating innate responses; aluminium salts are the most common human vaccine adjuvant and may act by inflammasome activation.
quote: Aluminum, in the form of various salts, is the most commonly used adjuvant in human vaccines and may work by causing inflammasome activation

fact: CpG, the TLR9 ligand, is used as an adjuvant in some hepatitis B virus vaccines.
quote: CpG, the ligand for TLR9, is used in some hepatitis B virus vaccines

fact: Adjuvants make DCs express more MHC molecules (signal 1), costimulators (signal 2) and cytokines, and migrate to lymph nodes.
quote: increase the expression of costimulators (signal 2) and cytokines needed for T-cell activation

fact: PAMP-activated DCs express costimulators and direct naive T cells to effector types such as Th1 or Th17; DCs bridge innate and adaptive immunity.
quote: DCs activated by microbial PAMPs also express membrane molecules called costimulators that promote T-cell responses.

fact: TNF-alpha stimulates DC migration from tissues to lymph nodes and maturation into highly costimulatory antigen-presenting cells.
quote: TNF-a also has a role in stimulating the migration of dendritic cells from their sites in peripheral tissues to the lymph node

fact: IgG-mediated phagocytosis shows that an adaptive product (antibody) engages innate effector cells.
quote: Antibody-dependent phagocytosis illustrates a link between innate and adaptive immunity

fact: IL-10 is made by and inhibits macrophages and DCs (negative feedback); loss-of-function IL-10 receptor mutations cause severe infantile colitis.
quote: Loss-of-function mutations in the IL-10 receptor result in severe colitis that develops in infancy.

fact: Antagonists of TNF, IL-1, IL-6 and IL-12 or their receptors are used to reduce inflammation in rheumatoid arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease and psoriasis.
quote: Antagonists against all of these cytokines or their receptors are used clinically to reduce inflammation

fact: In the airways, goblet cells secrete mucus, and beating cilia move the mucus outward to trap and eject pathogens.
quote: Beating of the cilia moves a continuous stream of mucus secreted by goblet cells (green) outward, trapping and ejecting potential pathogens

fact: The pentraxins include the short pentraxins CRP and SAP and the long pentraxin PTX3.
quote: include the short pentraxins, C-reactive protein (CRP) and serum amyloid P (SAP), and the long pentraxin PTX3
